records.source: בִּשְׁנַ֣ת אַחַ֗ת לְדָרְיָ֛וֶשׁ בֶּן־אֲחַשְׁוֵר֖וֹשׁ מִזֶּ֣רַע מָדָ֑י אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָמְלַ֔ךְ עַ֖ל מַלְכ֥וּת כַּשְׂדִּֽים׃
records.gloss: In year one of Darius son of Ahasuerus, of [the] descendants of Media, who was made king over [the] kingdom of [the] Chaldeans,
pieces: It was in the first year of Darius son of Ahasuerus, a Mede by descent, who had been made king over the realm of the Chaldeans.

L.1: In the first year of Darius son of Ahasuerus, of the descendants of the Medes, who was made king over the kingdom of the Chaldeans,

R.1: Darius son of Ahasuerus was a Mede. He had been made king over the kingdom of the Babylonians. In his first year as king,

decisions.choice: Darius son of Ahasuerus, a Mede: the king of 6:1
decisions.reason: Darius the Mede is the king who received the kingdom when Babylon fell (6:1). No such king is known outside the book of Daniel, and he is identified in different ways: as a throne name of Cyrus himself, as Gubaru (Cyrus's governor of Babylon), or otherwise; see the note at 6:1. Ahasuerus is the name the Hebrew Bible gives to the Persian king Xerxes (Esther 1:1); this Ahasuerus is not otherwise known.

decisions.choice: who was made king: he received the kingship from another
decisions.reason: The verb is passive: Darius was made king, by Cyrus or by God. Compare 6:1, "Darius the Mede received the kingdom". The year is about 539-538 BC, the first year after the fall of Babylon.

decisions.choice: the Babylonians (R)
decisions.reason: The table for Daniel gives "Chaldeans" at Literal and Balanced and "Babylonians" at Readable where the word means the people. The sentence runs on into verse 2; Literal ends this verse with a comma, and Balanced makes it a sentence of its own.

records.heading: Daniel's prayer and the seventy sevens

records.source: בִּשְׁנַ֤ת אַחַת֙ לְמָלְכ֔וֹ אֲנִי֙ דָּֽנִיֵּ֔אל בִּינֹ֖תִי בַּסְּפָרִ֑ים מִסְפַּ֣ר הַשָּׁנִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֤ה דְבַר־יְהוָה֙ אֶל־יִרְמִיָ֣ה הַנָּבִ֔יא לְמַלֹּ֛אות לְחָרְב֥וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם שִׁבְעִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: in year one of his reigning, I, Daniel, observed in the scrolls the number of the years, which came the word of Yahweh to Jeremiah the prophet, to complete for [the] desolations of Jerusalem: seventy years.
pieces: In the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, came to understand from the scriptures the number of years that, according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to the prophet Jeremiah, must pass before the desolation of Jerusalem would come to an end: seventy years.

L.2: in the first year of his reign I, Daniel, perceived in the scrolls the number of the years which, according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to Jeremiah the prophet, were to be completed for the desolations of Jerusalem: seventy years.

R.2: I, Daniel, was studying the scrolls. I read the message that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had given to the prophet Jeremiah. It said that Jerusalem would lie in ruins for seventy years.

decisions.choice: seventy years: the word of the LORD to Jeremiah
decisions.reason: Jeremiah said that the land would be a ruin and the nations would serve the king of Babylon for seventy years (Jeremiah 25:11-12), and that after seventy years for Babylon the LORD would bring his people home (Jeremiah 29:10). 2 Chronicles 36:21 links the seventy years with the sabbath rests the land had missed (Leviticus 26:34-35). Daniel, in the year Babylon fell, sees that the time is nearly over, and he prays.

decisions.choice: the scrolls: the written books, including Jeremiah's prophecy
decisions.reason: The word means writings or books. Jeremiah's words were written on scrolls (Jeremiah 29:1; 36:2), and Daniel reads them as a word of the LORD.

decisions.choice: the desolations of Jerusalem: the ruined state of the city
decisions.reason: The word is from the root used for desolation throughout these chapters (8:13; 9:17-18, 26-27). Jerusalem had lain in ruins since 587 BC.

decisions.choice: the scriptures (B); the scrolls (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "scriptures", since the scrolls are the written word of the prophets; Readable keeps "scrolls". Readable makes the long sentence into three and drops the date, which the previous verse gives.

records.source: וָאֶתְּנָ֣ה אֶת־פָּנַ֗י אֶל־אֲדֹנָי֙ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים לְבַקֵּ֥שׁ תְּפִלָּ֖ה וְתַחֲנוּנִ֑ים בְּצ֖וֹם וְשַׂ֥ק וָאֵֽפֶר׃
records.gloss: And I set my face to the Lord God, to seek prayer and supplications with fasting and sackcloth and ashes.
pieces: So I turned to the Lord God, seeking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in prayer and pleading for mercy, with fasting, in sackcloth and ashes.

L.3: And I set my face toward the Lord God, to seek [him by] prayer and pleas for mercy, with fasting and sackcloth and ashes.

R.3: So I turned to the Lord God and prayed. I begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for mercy. I fasted, wore rough clothing and put ashes on my head.

decisions.choice: I set my face toward the Lord God: I turned to him with resolve
decisions.reason: To set one's face is to turn toward something with fixed purpose (2 Kings 12:18; Jeremiah 42:15). Daniel may also have faced toward Jerusalem, as he did in 6:11 (1 Kings 8:48).

decisions.choice: fasting, sackcloth and ashes: signs of grief and repentance
decisions.reason: Sackcloth was rough cloth of goat's hair worn in mourning, and ashes were put on the head or sat in (Nehemiah 9:1; Jonah 3:6; Esther 4:1). Together with fasting they show humble sorrow before God.

decisions.choice: the Lord: the title Adonai
decisions.reason: Daniel calls on God by the title "Lord" (Adonai) here and throughout the prayer (verses 4, 7, 9, 15-17, 19), and by the divine name in verses 4, 8, 10, 13-14 and 20.

decisions.choice: wore rough clothing and put ashes on my head (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what sackcloth and ashes were (m2).

records.source: וָֽאֶתְפַּֽלְלָ֛ה לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהַ֖י וָאֶתְוַדֶּ֑ה וָאֹֽמְרָ֗ה אָנָּ֤א אֲדֹנָי֙ הָאֵ֤ל הַגָּדוֹל֙ וְהַנּוֹרָ֔א שֹׁמֵ֤ר הַבְּרִית֙ וְֽהַחֶ֔סֶד לְאֹהֲבָ֖יו וּלְשֹׁמְרֵ֥י מִצְוֺתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And I prayed to Yahweh my God and confessed, and I said: Ah, Lord, the God, the great and the awesome, keeping the covenant and the loyal love for those loving him and for those keeping his commandments,
pieces: I prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God and confessed, saying, "Lord, the great and awesome God, who keeps {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love with those who love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments,

L.4: And I prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God and made confession, and said, "Ah, Lord, the great and awesome God, who keeps the covenant and the loyal love with those who love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments,

R.4: I prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God and confessed our sins. I said, "Lord, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the great and awesome God. You keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} covenant and show faithful love to those who love {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and obey {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands.

decisions.choice: the great and awesome God, who keeps covenant and loyal love: Deuteronomy 7:9, 21
decisions.reason: The words are those of Deuteronomy 7:9 ("the faithful God, who keeps covenant and loyal love with those who love him and keep his commandments") and 7:21 ("a great and awesome God"). Nehemiah's prayers open in the same words (Nehemiah 1:5; 9:32). Daniel's prayer is built from the language of the law and the prophets.

decisions.choice: hesed: loyal love, God's faithful kindness within the covenant
decisions.reason: The word means steadfast, faithful love that keeps a bond. Here it is paired with "the covenant": God keeps his covenant and the love he has promised in it.

decisions.choice: Ah: a word of earnest pleading
decisions.reason: The word opens a plea or confession with urgency (Nehemiah 1:5, 11; Jonah 1:14).

decisions.choice: confessed: the prayer is a confession of the people's sin
decisions.reason: The prayer (verses 4-19) confesses the sin of Israel, says that God was right to punish, and asks him to act for his own name's sake. It is like the prayers of Ezra 9 and Nehemiah 1 and 9, and asks for what Solomon's prayer foresaw (1 Kings 8:46-53).

decisions.choice: loyal love (L, B); faithful love (R)
decisions.reason: Hesed follows the wording set for the prophets: "loyal love" at Literal and Balanced, "faithful love" at Readable. Nehemiah 1:5 and Deuteronomy 7:9, which this verse echoes, were published with "steadfast love" at Literal; the founder's ruling on quotations of Exodus 34:6 is still open, and this wording follows the prophets until it is given.

decisions.choice: you, your, him, his for God (deity pronoun)
decisions.reason: Daniel's prayer speaks to God as "you" and about him as "he"; every such pronoun takes the deity_pronoun setting, except at the start of a sentence. The prayer is set in double quotation marks from here to the end of verse 19.

decisions.choice: the LORD (divine name); Lord (Adonai); no "O"
decisions.reason: The divine name is written as a setting span. "Ah" at Literal keeps the pleading word; Balanced and Readable begin with the vocative "Lord" alone, with no "O", as the vocative is written in the prophets.

records.source: חָטָ֥אנוּ וְעָוִ֖ינוּ הִרְשַׁ֣עְנוּ וּמָרָ֑דְנוּ וְס֥וֹר מִמִּצְוֺתֶ֖ךָ וּמִמִּשְׁפָּטֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: We have sinned and done iniquity, and acted wickedly and rebelled, and turned aside from your commandments and from your judgments.
pieces: We have sinned and done wrong; we have been wicked and have rebelled, turning away from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commandments and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rules.

L.5: We have sinned and committed iniquity and acted wickedly and rebelled, turning aside from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commandments and from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgments.

R.5: We have sinned and done wrong. We have been wicked and have turned against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. We have turned away from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} laws.

decisions.choice: we have sinned, done wrong, acted wickedly: the confession of 1 Kings 8:47
decisions.reason: Solomon's prayer gave these words as the confession Israel would make in exile (1 Kings 8:47; compare Psalm 106:6). Daniel makes it, and adds "and rebelled".

decisions.choice: judgments: the ordinances, God's rulings in the law
decisions.reason: The word means decisions or rulings, and in the law the specific rules God gave (Deuteronomy 4:1).

decisions.choice: your (deity pronoun)
decisions.reason: The pronouns for God take the deity_pronoun setting. Balanced says "been wicked" for the third verb.

records.source: וְלֹ֤א שָׁמַ֨עְנוּ֙ אֶל־עֲבָדֶ֣יךָ הַנְּבִיאִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר דִּבְּרוּ֙ בְּשִׁמְךָ֔ אֶל־מְלָכֵ֥ינוּ שָׂרֵ֖ינוּ וַאֲבֹתֵ֑ינוּ וְאֶ֖ל כָּל־עַ֥ם הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And not we have listened to your servants the prophets, who spoke in your name to our kings, our leaders and our fathers and to all [the] people of the land.
pieces: We did not listen to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants the prophets when they spoke in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name to our kings, our officials and our ancestors, and to all the people of the land.

L.6: And we have not listened to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants the prophets, who in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name spoke to our kings, our princes and our fathers, and to the whole people of the land.

R.6: We have not listened to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants the prophets. They spoke for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to our kings and leaders and ancestors, and to all the people in the land.

decisions.choice: your servants the prophets: the phrase of Jeremiah and Kings
decisions.reason: The phrase is common in Jeremiah (7:25; 25:4; 26:5) and in Kings (2 Kings 17:13, 23). God sent his prophets again and again, and the people did not listen.

decisions.choice: princes: the officials of the royal court
decisions.reason: The word means leaders or officials, the men who served under the king (Jeremiah 26:10-12).

decisions.choice: servants (all levels); princes (L), officials (B), leaders (R); fathers (L), ancestors (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Your servants the prophets" is kept at every level, as the prophets' "my servants" is published in Jeremiah 7:25. Sar for human officials follows the wording settled for the prophets (officials, leaders); Literal keeps "princes" here, as Nehemiah 9:32 does in a list of the same kind.

decisions.choice: your (deity pronoun)
decisions.reason: The pronouns for God take the deity_pronoun setting. Readable says "spoke for you" for "spoke in your name".

records.source: לְךָ֤ אֲדֹנָי֙ הַצְּדָקָ֔ה וְלָ֛נוּ בֹּ֥שֶׁת הַפָּנִ֖ים כַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה לְאִ֤ישׁ יְהוּדָה֙ וּלְיוֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרֽוּשָׁלִַ֔ם וּֽלְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֞ל הַקְּרֹבִ֣ים וְהָרְחֹקִ֗ים בְּכָל־הָֽאֲרָצוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִדַּחְתָּ֣ם שָׁ֔ם בְּמַעֲלָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר מָֽעֲלוּ־בָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: To you, Lord, [belongs] the righteousness, and to us shame of the faces as this day, to [the] men of Judah and to [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem and to all Israel, the near and the far, in all the lands where you have banished them there, in their unfaithfulness which they acted unfaithfully against you.
pieces: Lord, righteousness belongs to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, but to us belongs open shame, as it is today: to the people of Judah, the residents of Jerusalem and all Israel, near and far away, in all the lands where {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have scattered them because of the unfaithfulness they have shown {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.7: To {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord, belongs righteousness, but to us shame of face, as on this day: to the men of Judah, to those who live in Jerusalem, and to all Israel, those near and those far away, in all the lands to which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have driven them, because of their unfaithfulness which they committed against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.7: Lord, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} always do what is right. But we are covered with shame, as we are today. This is true of the people of Judah and of Jerusalem, and of all Israel, both near and far away. You have scattered them in all the countries of the world, because they have been unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: to you belongs righteousness, to us shame: God is in the right; the people are guilty
decisions.reason: Daniel does not accuse God for the ruin of Jerusalem. He confesses that God has been right in all he has done, and that the shame on the people's faces is deserved (verse 14; Nehemiah 9:33; Ezra 9:15).

decisions.choice: shame of face, as at this day: the open disgrace they bear now
decisions.reason: Shame shows on the face (2 Chronicles 32:21; Jeremiah 7:19). "As at this day" means as can be seen now (Deuteronomy 29:27; Jeremiah 44:22).

decisions.choice: unfaithfulness: breach of trust against God
decisions.reason: The word means acting treacherously, breaking faith, as with something that belongs to God (Leviticus 26:40; 1 Chronicles 10:13).

decisions.choice: righteousness (L, B); you always do what is right (R); men of Judah (L), people of Judah (B, R)
decisions.reason: Righteousness follows the Isaiah table. Readable says what it means of God here (m1). The men of Judah means its people, and Balanced and Readable say so; it is not a gender span because it names the people of one land.

decisions.choice: you (deity pronoun)
decisions.reason: Daniel's prayer speaks to God as "you" and about him as "he"; every such pronoun takes the deity_pronoun setting, except at the start of a sentence.

records.source: יְהוָ֗ה לָ֚נוּ בֹּ֣שֶׁת הַפָּנִ֔ים לִמְלָכֵ֥ינוּ לְשָׂרֵ֖ינוּ וְלַאֲבֹתֵ֑ינוּ אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָטָ֖אנוּ לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Yahweh, to us [belongs] shame of the faces, to our kings, to our leaders and to our fathers, who have sinned against you.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, open shame belongs to us, to our kings, our officials and our ancestors, because we have sinned against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.8: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, shame of face [belongs] to us, to our kings, to our princes and to our fathers, for we have sinned against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.8: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, we are covered with shame, and so are our kings, our leaders and our ancestors. We have sinned against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: because we have sinned: the reason for the shame
decisions.reason: The word that begins the last clause gives the reason for the shame: "because" or "for". The kings, leaders and fathers are counted together with "us" in the sin.

decisions.choice: LORD as a vocative, with no "O"
decisions.reason: The divine name addressed directly is written as the vocative span with no "O", as in the Psalms and the prophets.

decisions.choice: you (deity pronoun)
decisions.reason: Daniel's prayer speaks to God as "you" and about him as "he"; every such pronoun takes the deity_pronoun setting, except at the start of a sentence.

records.source: לַֽאדֹנָ֣י אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ הָרַחֲמִ֖ים וְהַסְּלִח֑וֹת כִּ֥י מָרַ֖דְנוּ בּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: To [the] Lord our God [belong] the compassions and the forgivenesses, for we have rebelled against him,
pieces: But the Lord our God is merciful and forgiving, even though we have rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.9: To the Lord our God belong compassion and forgiveness, for we have rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}

R.9: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord our God, are kind and forgiving, even though we have turned against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: for we have rebelled: though, or because, we have rebelled
decisions.reason: The small word that joins the clauses can mean "for" or "though". God's compassion and forgiveness are all the more needed, and all the more great, because the people have rebelled.

decisions.choice: compassion and forgiveness: both plural in the Hebrew
decisions.reason: Both words are plural, a way of speaking of abundant mercy and many acts of forgiveness (Nehemiah 9:17, "a God of forgivenesses"; Psalm 130:4).

decisions.choice: no closing punctuation at the end of the verse (L)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence runs into verse 10, and Literal joins them with no full stop.

decisions.choice: you, Lord our God (R)
decisions.reason: Daniel speaks about God here in the third person, as in verses 10-14, though he is praying to him. Readable turns it to "you" so that it is clear Daniel is still speaking to God; Literal and Balanced keep "him". The pronoun takes the deity_pronoun setting at every level.

records.source: וְלֹ֣א שָׁמַ֔עְנוּ בְּק֖וֹל יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ לָלֶ֤כֶת בְּתֽוֹרֹתָיו֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣ן לְפָנֵ֔ינוּ בְּיַ֖ד עֲבָדָ֥יו הַנְּבִיאִֽים׃
records.gloss: and not we have listened to [the] voice of Yahweh our God, to walk in his instructions which he set before us by [the] hand of his servants the prophets.
pieces: We have not obeyed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God or lived by the instructions {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} set before us through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants the prophets.

L.10: and we have not listened to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, to walk in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} instructions which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} set before us by the hand of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants the prophets.

R.10: We have not obeyed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God. We have not lived by the teachings {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave us through {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants the prophets.

decisions.choice: listened to the voice: obeyed
decisions.reason: To listen to someone's voice is to obey them (Deuteronomy 13:5; Jeremiah 7:23).

decisions.choice: instructions: God's teachings, the torah
decisions.reason: The plural of the word torah means God's instructions or laws (Exodus 18:16, 20; Jeremiah 44:23). "By the hand of" means through the prophets as his messengers.

decisions.choice: instructions (L, B); teachings (R)
decisions.reason: Torah follows the Isaiah table, "instruction" and "teaching", in the plural here. Readable turns the third person to "you", as in verse 9.

records.source: וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל עָֽבְרוּ֙ אֶת־תּ֣וֹרָתֶ֔ךָ וְס֕וֹר לְבִלְתִּ֖י שְׁמ֣וֹעַ בְּקֹלֶ֑ךָ וַתִּתַּ֨ךְ עָלֵ֜ינוּ הָאָלָ֣ה וְהַשְּׁבֻעָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר כְּתוּבָה֙ בְּתוֹרַת֙ מֹשֶׁ֣ה עֶֽבֶד־הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים כִּ֥י חָטָ֖אנוּ לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And all Israel have transgressed your law and turned aside, not to listen to your voice; and has been poured on us the curse and the oath which [is] written in [the] law of Moses the servant of God, for we have sinned against him.
pieces: All Israel has broken {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} law and turned away, refusing to obey {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. So the curse and the oath that are written in the law of Moses, the servant of God, have been poured out on us, because we have sinned against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.11: And all Israel has transgressed {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} law and turned aside, not listening to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} voice; so the curse and the oath that are written in the law of Moses the servant of God have been poured out on us, because we have sinned against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.11: All the people of Israel have broken {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} law and turned away. They have refused to obey {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. So the curses that are written in the law of Moses, God's servant, have been poured out on us. That happened because we have sinned against God.

decisions.choice: the curse and the oath written in the law of Moses: Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 28-29
decisions.reason: The law of Moses ends its covenant with blessings for obedience and curses for disobedience, sealed with an oath (Leviticus 26:14-39; Deuteronomy 28:15-68; 29:11, 19-20). Exile and the ruin of the land are among the curses (Deuteronomy 28:36, 64; 29:27). Daniel sees them fulfilled.

decisions.choice: your law: God's torah, here the law given through Moses
decisions.reason: Here the word means the written law as a whole, as "the law of Moses" later in the verse shows.

decisions.choice: law (all levels); the law of Moses the servant of God (all levels)
decisions.reason: Torah is "instruction" in the prophets' table, but "the law of Moses" is the wording published for this phrase (Ezra 3:2; Malachi 3:22), and "your law" here means the same written law, so every level says "law". "Servant" is kept at every level, as in Malachi 3:22.

decisions.choice: the curses (R); God (R)
decisions.reason: Readable joins "the curse and the oath" as "the curses" and names God where the Hebrew says "him".

records.source: וַיָּ֜קֶם אֶת־דְּבָר֣וֹ׀אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֣ר עָלֵ֗ינוּ וְעַ֤ל שֹֽׁפְטֵ֨ינוּ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שְׁפָט֔וּנוּ לְהָבִ֥יא עָלֵ֖ינוּ רָעָ֣ה גְדֹלָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־נֶעֶשְׂתָ֗ה תַּ֚חַת כָּל־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר נֶעֶשְׂתָ֖ה בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: And he has carried out his words which he spoke against us and against our judges who judged us, by bringing on us calamity great, which not has been done under all the heavens as has been done in Jerusalem.
pieces: He has carried out the warnings {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke against us and against our rulers who governed us, by bringing on us a great disaster. Nowhere under heaven has anything been done like what was done to Jerusalem.

L.12: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has fulfilled {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke against us and against our judges who judged us, bringing on us great calamity; for under the whole heaven nothing has been done like what has been done to Jerusalem.

R.12: You did what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} said {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} would do to us and to our rulers. You brought a terrible disaster on us. Nothing anywhere in the world has ever been as bad as what happened to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: our judges who judged us: our rulers
decisions.reason: "Judges" here means all who governed Israel, kings and officials, as in Psalm 2:10 and Amos 2:3.

decisions.choice: nothing like what has been done to Jerusalem: the language of Lamentations
decisions.reason: Lamentations asks whether there is any sorrow like Jerusalem's (Lamentations 1:12; 2:13). The calamity of 587 BC was the curse of the covenant in full.

decisions.choice: the warnings (B); what you said you would do (R)
decisions.reason: The words God spoke against them are the warnings of the law and the prophets; Balanced and Readable say so. Readable turns the third person to "you", as in verse 9.

records.source: כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר כָּתוּב֙ בְּתוֹרַ֣ת מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֵ֛ת כָּל־הָרָעָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את בָּ֣אָה עָלֵ֑ינוּ וְלֹֽא־חִלִּ֜ינוּ אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י׀יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ לָשׁוּב֙ מֵֽעֲוֺנֵ֔נוּ וּלְהַשְׂכִּ֖יל בַּאֲמִתֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: As [is] written in [the] law of Moses, all the calamity this has come on us; and not we have entreated the face of Yahweh our God by turning from our iniquity and by giving attention to your truth.
pieces: All this disaster has come on us, as the law of Moses says it would. Yet we have not pleaded for the favor of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God by turning away from our sins and paying attention to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} truth.

L.13: As it is written in the law of Moses, all this calamity has come upon us; yet we have not entreated the face of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God by turning back from our iniquities and paying attention to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} truth.

R.13: Everything happened to us just as it was written in the law of Moses. All this disaster came on us. But we still have not asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God to be kind to us. We have not turned away from our sins or paid attention to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} truth.

decisions.choice: entreat the face of the LORD: seek his favor
decisions.reason: The phrase means literally "soften the face" of someone, that is, seek to win his favor by pleading (Exodus 32:11; Jeremiah 26:19).

decisions.choice: your truth: your faithfulness, the truth of your word
decisions.reason: The word means truth and faithfulness. They have not given heed to God's true word and his faithfulness to it. Some take it as "insight into your truth".

decisions.choice: iniquities (L); sins (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word for iniquity follows the Isaiah table: "iniquity" at Literal, "sin" at Balanced and Readable. The Hebrew is singular, used for the whole; Literal makes it plural to match "our".

records.source: וַיִּשְׁקֹ֤ד יְהוָה֙ עַל־הָ֣רָעָ֔ה וַיְבִיאֶ֖הָ עָלֵ֑ינוּ כִּֽי־צַדִּ֞יק יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ עַל־כָּל־מַֽעֲשָׂיו֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖עְנוּ בְּקֹלֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And Yahweh kept watch over the calamity and brought it on us, for righteous [is] Yahweh our God in all his deeds which he has done, and not we have listened to his voice.
pieces: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} kept the disaster ready and brought it on us, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God is righteous in everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does, yet we have not obeyed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.14: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} kept watch over the calamity and brought it on us, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God is righteous in all the works {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done, but we have not listened to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice.

R.14: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was ready to bring this disaster on us, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought it. {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God is always right in everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does. But we did not obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: the LORD kept watch over the calamity: the word of Jeremiah 1:12
decisions.reason: The verb is the one in the LORD's wordplay with Jeremiah: "I am watching over my word to perform it" (Jeremiah 1:12), and "I am watching over them for harm" (Jeremiah 44:27). God was ready to bring the disaster he had threatened, and he did.

decisions.choice: the LORD our God is righteous: the judgment was just
decisions.reason: As in verse 7, the prayer confesses that God was in the right in what he did.

decisions.choice: kept the disaster ready (B); was ready to bring (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "kept watch over"; Balanced and Readable give the sense of the verb here (m1). Balanced and Readable say "obeyed" for "listened to his voice".

records.source: וְעַתָּ֣ה׀אֲדֹנָ֣י אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ אֲשֶׁר֩ הוֹצֵ֨אתָ אֶֽת־עַמְּךָ֜ מֵאֶ֤רֶץ מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ בְּיָ֣ד חֲזָקָ֔ה וַתַּֽעַשׂ־לְךָ֥ שֵׁ֖ם כַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה חָטָ֖אנוּ רָשָֽׁעְנוּ׃
records.gloss: And now, Lord our God, who brought out your people from [the] land of Egypt with a hand strong, and made for yourself a name as this day: we have sinned, we have acted wickedly.
pieces: Now, Lord our God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} rescued {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people from the land of Egypt with a mighty hand and made a name for {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} that lasts to this day. We have sinned; we have done wrong.

L.15: And now, Lord our God, who brought {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people out from the land of Egypt with a strong hand and made a name for {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}, as at this day, we have sinned, we have acted wickedly.

R.15: Lord our God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} used {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great power to bring {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people out of Egypt. Because of that, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are famous even today. But we have sinned. We have done wicked things.

decisions.choice: brought out of Egypt with a mighty hand, and made a name for yourself
decisions.reason: The prayer turns from confession to request by recalling the exodus (Exodus 32:11; Deuteronomy 7:8). By rescuing Israel from Egypt, God made his name known among the nations (Jeremiah 32:20-21; Nehemiah 9:10). Daniel appeals to that name in verses 17-19.

decisions.choice: with a mighty hand: by great power
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power (Exodus 13:9; Deuteronomy 26:8).

decisions.choice: your, yourself (deity pronoun)
decisions.reason: Daniel's prayer speaks to God as "you" and about him as "he"; every such pronoun takes the deity_pronoun setting, except at the start of a sentence. Readable says "with your great power" for "with a mighty hand" (m2).

records.source: אֲדֹנָ֗י כְּכָל־צִדְקֹתֶ֨ךָ֙ יָֽשָׁב־נָ֤א אַפְּךָ֙ וַחֲמָ֣תְךָ֔ מֵעִֽירְךָ֥ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם הַר־קָדְשֶׁ֑ךָ כִּ֤י בַחֲטָאֵ֨ינוּ֙ וּבַעֲוֺנ֣וֹת אֲבֹתֵ֔ינוּ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֧ם וְעַמְּךָ֛ לְחֶרְפָּ֖ה לְכָל־סְבִיבֹתֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: Lord, according to all your righteousnesses, let turn back, please, your anger and your wrath from your city Jerusalem, your holy mountain; for by our sins and by the iniquities of our fathers, Jerusalem and your people [are] a reproach to all around us.
pieces: Lord, in keeping with all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteous acts, turn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} fury away from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} city Jerusalem, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy mountain. Because of our sins and the wrongdoing of our ancestors, Jerusalem and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people have become an object of scorn to all the nations around us.

L.16: Lord, according to all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteous acts, let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wrath turn away, please, from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} city Jerusalem, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy mountain. For by our sins and by the iniquities of our fathers, Jerusalem and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people have been made a reproach among all our neighbors.

R.16: Lord, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have always done what is right. So please stop being angry with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} city Jerusalem, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy mountain. Because of our sins and the sins of our ancestors, all the people around us make fun of Jerusalem and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people.

decisions.choice: your righteous acts: the saving deeds that show God's righteousness
decisions.reason: The plural of "righteousness" means God's acts of righteousness, his saving deeds for his people (Judges 5:11; 1 Samuel 12:7; Micah 6:5). Daniel asks God to act now as he has acted before.

decisions.choice: your holy mountain: Mount Zion, where the temple stood
decisions.reason: Jerusalem and its temple mount are "your holy mountain" in the Psalms and prophets (Psalm 2:6; Isaiah 11:9; Joel 2:1).

decisions.choice: a disgrace to all around us: mocked by the neighboring nations
decisions.reason: The word means a reproach, an object of scorn (Psalm 79:4; Lamentations 5:1). The nations' mockery of Jerusalem dishonors the God whose city it is.

decisions.choice: righteous acts (L, B); you have always done what is right (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced say "righteous acts" for the plural (m1); Readable says it as a sentence.

decisions.choice: your (deity pronoun)
decisions.reason: Daniel's prayer speaks to God as "you" and about him as "he"; every such pronoun takes the deity_pronoun setting, except at the start of a sentence.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֣ה׀שְׁמַ֣ע אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ אֶל־תְּפִלַּ֤ת עַבְדְּךָ֙ וְאֶל־תַּ֣חֲנוּנָ֔יו וְהָאֵ֣ר פָּנֶ֔יךָ עַל־מִקְדָּשְׁךָ֖ הַשָּׁמֵ֑ם לְמַ֖עַן אֲדֹנָֽי׃
records.gloss: And now listen, our God, to [the] prayer of your servant and to his supplications, and make shine your face on your sanctuary, the desolate, for [the] sake of [the] Lord.
pieces: Now, our God, listen to the prayer and the pleas of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant. For {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own sake, Lord, look with favor on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sanctuary, which lies in ruins.

L.17: And now listen, our God, to the prayer of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant and to his pleas for mercy, and make {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face shine upon {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sanctuary, which is desolate, for the Lord's sake.

R.17: Now, our God, listen to my prayer. I am {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant. Hear me as I beg {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for mercy. Lord, for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own sake, be kind to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} temple, which lies in ruins.

decisions.choice: make your face shine: look with favor
decisions.reason: The words come from the priestly blessing: "The LORD make his face shine on you" (Numbers 6:25), and from the prayer of Psalm 80:4, 8, 20. A shining face is a sign of favor.

decisions.choice: for the Lord's sake: for your own sake, Lord
decisions.reason: Daniel speaks of God by his title in the third person, as one would before a king. Some ancient translations read "for your sake, Lord". Either way, he asks God to act for the sake of his own name and honor, not because of anything the people deserve (verses 18-19).

decisions.choice: for your own sake, Lord (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the third person, "for the Lord's sake"; Balanced and Readable say it as Daniel means it (m2). Readable says "look with favor" plainly as "be kind to".

decisions.choice: your servant (all levels); my prayer, I am your servant (R)
decisions.reason: Daniel speaks of himself politely as "your servant", as Solomon does (1 Kings 8:28); every level keeps "servant", and Readable also says "I" and "me". The pronouns for God take the deity_pronoun setting; "his pleas" is Daniel's own.

records.source: הַטֵּ֨ה אֱלֹהַ֥י׀אָזְנְךָ֮ וּֽשֲׁמָע֒ פְּקַ֣ח עֵינֶ֗יךָ וּרְאֵה֙ שֹֽׁמְמֹתֵ֔ינוּ וְהָעִ֕יר אֲשֶׁר־נִקְרָ֥א שִׁמְךָ֖ עָלֶ֑יהָ כִּ֣י׀לֹ֣א עַל־צִדְקֹתֵ֗ינוּ אֲנַ֨חְנוּ מַפִּילִ֤ים תַּחֲנוּנֵ֨ינוּ֙ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ כִּ֖י עַל־רַחֲמֶ֥יךָ הָרַבִּֽים׃
records.gloss: Incline, my God, your ear and hear; open your eyes and see our desolations and the city over which your name is called; for not on [account of] our righteousnesses we [are] presenting our supplications before you, but on [account of] your compassions the great.
pieces: Turn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ear to us, my God, and hear. Open {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes and see our ruins and the city that bears {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name. We do not bring our pleas to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} because we are righteous, but because of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great mercy.

L.18: Incline {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ear, my God, and hear! Open {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes and look at our desolations and at the city over which {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name is called. For we are not presenting our pleas before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} because of our righteous deeds, but because of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great compassion.

R.18: My God, please listen to us. Open {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes and see how we and our city are ruined. This city belongs to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. We are not asking {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for help because we have done what is right. We are asking because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are so kind.

decisions.choice: incline your ear, open your eyes: pay attention and take note
decisions.reason: The pictures come from prayers like Hezekiah's (2 Kings 19:16; Isaiah 37:17) and Solomon's (1 Kings 8:29, 52).

decisions.choice: the city over which your name is called: the city that belongs to you
decisions.reason: To have one's name called over something is to own it (2 Samuel 12:28; Jeremiah 7:10). Jerusalem is God's own city, so its ruin touches his honor.

decisions.choice: presenting our pleas: literally, making them fall before you
decisions.reason: The idiom pictures the pleas laid down before God, as one bows down before a king (Jeremiah 36:7; 42:9).

decisions.choice: your, you (deity pronoun)
decisions.reason: Daniel's prayer speaks to God as "you" and about him as "he"; every such pronoun takes the deity_pronoun setting, except at the start of a sentence.

records.source: אֲדֹנָ֤י׀שְׁמָ֨עָה֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י׀סְלָ֔חָה אֲדֹנָ֛י הַֽקֲשִׁ֥יבָה וַעֲשֵׂ֖ה אַל־תְּאַחַ֑ר לְמַֽעֲנְךָ֣ אֱלֹהַ֔י כִּֽי־שִׁמְךָ֣ נִקְרָ֔א עַל־עִירְךָ֖ וְעַל־עַמֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Lord, hear! Lord, forgive! Lord, give attention and act! Do not delay, for your own sake, my God, for your name is called over your city and over your people.
pieces: Lord, listen! Lord, forgive! Lord, take note and act! Do not delay, my God, for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own sake, since {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} city and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people bear {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name."

L.19: Lord, hear! Lord, forgive! Lord, pay attention and act! Do not delay, for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own sake, my God, because {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name is called over {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} city and over {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people."

R.19: Lord, listen! Lord, forgive us! Lord, pay attention and do something! My God, do not wait any longer. Do it for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own sake, because {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} city and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people belong to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

decisions.choice: Lord ... Lord ... Lord: three short cries
decisions.reason: The prayer ends in three cries, each beginning with "Lord", and a plea not to delay. The urgency of the words matches the hope of verse 2: the seventy years are nearly complete.

decisions.choice: your name is called over your city and your people: they belong to you
decisions.reason: As in verse 18. The appeal rests on God's ownership of the city and people, and on his name (verses 15, 17).

decisions.choice: your (deity pronoun)
decisions.reason: Daniel's prayer speaks to God as "you" and about him as "he"; every such pronoun takes the deity_pronoun setting, except at the start of a sentence. The prayer's closing quotation mark comes at the end of this verse.

records.source: וְע֨וֹד אֲנִ֤י מְדַבֵּר֙ וּמִתְפַּלֵּ֔ל וּמִתְוַדֶּה֙ חַטָּאתִ֔י וְחַטַּ֖את עַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּמַפִּ֣יל תְּחִנָּתִ֗י לִפְנֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהַ֔י עַ֖ל הַר־קֹ֥דֶשׁ אֱלֹהָֽי׃
records.gloss: And while I [was] speaking and praying and confessing my sin and [the] sin of my people Israel, and presenting my supplication before Yahweh my God for the holy mountain of my God,
pieces: While I was still speaking and praying, confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel, and bringing my plea before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God on behalf of the holy mountain of my God,

L.20: And while I was still speaking and praying, confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel and laying my plea before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God concerning the holy mountain of my God,

R.20: I was still praying. I was confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel. I was asking {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God to help Jerusalem, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy mountain.

decisions.choice: while I was still speaking: the answer comes during the prayer
decisions.reason: Verses 20-21 make one sentence: Gabriel arrives while Daniel is still praying. Compare Isaiah 65:24: "while they are still speaking, I will hear".

decisions.choice: Jerusalem, his holy mountain (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the holy mountain (verse 16). "His" there is God's and takes the deity_pronoun setting.

records.source: וְע֛וֹד אֲנִ֥י מְדַבֵּ֖ר בַּתְּפִלָּ֑ה וְהָאִ֣ישׁ גַּבְרִיאֵ֡ל אֲשֶׁר֩ רָאִ֨יתִי בֶחָז֤וֹן בַּתְּחִלָּה֙ מֻעָ֣ף בִּיעָ֔ף נֹגֵ֣עַ אֵלַ֔י כְּעֵ֖ת מִנְחַת־עָֽרֶב׃
records.gloss: and while I [was] speaking in prayer, and the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, being made to fly in flight, approaching to me about [the] time of [the] offering of [the] evening.
pieces: while I was still praying, Gabriel came to me in swift flight about the hour of the evening offering. He was the man I had seen in the earlier vision.

L.21: while I was still speaking in prayer, the man Gabriel, the one I had seen at the beginning in the vision, reached me in swift flight about the hour of the evening offering.

R.21: While I was still praying, Gabriel came to me. He was the one who looked like a man, whom I had seen in the earlier vision. He came flying swiftly to me, at about the time of the evening sacrifice.

decisions.choice: in swift flight: or, when I was utterly weary
decisions.reason: The two words can be read as from the verb "to fly" ("made to fly swiftly") or from the verb "to be weary" ("being greatly wearied"). If the second, it may describe Daniel's exhaustion (compare 8:27) rather than Gabriel. Angels in the Old Testament are not usually pictured with wings, but the seraphim fly (Isaiah 6:2, 6). Some ancient translations read "flying".

decisions.choice: the time of the evening offering: mid-afternoon, a set hour of prayer
decisions.reason: The evening offering was made at the temple in the late afternoon (Exodus 29:39-41; 1 Kings 18:36). The temple lay in ruins, but the hour remained a time of prayer (Ezra 9:5; Psalm 141:2).

decisions.choice: the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning: 8:15-16
decisions.reason: Gabriel first appeared to Daniel with the appearance of a man (8:15-16). "Man" here describes how he appeared, not what he is.

decisions.choice: Gabriel, the man (B); the one who looked like a man (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the man" means (m3).

records.source: וַיָּ֖בֶן וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר עִמִּ֑י וַיֹּאמַ֕ר דָּנִיֵּ֕אל עַתָּ֥ה יָצָ֖אתִי לְהַשְׂכִּילְךָ֥ בִינָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he gave understanding and spoke with me and said: Daniel, now I have come out to make you wise [in] understanding.
pieces: He explained things to me and said, "Daniel, I have now come to give you insight and understanding.

L.22: And he instructed me and spoke with me and said, "Daniel, I have now come out to give you insight and understanding.

R.22: He explained things to me. He said, "Daniel, I have come to help you understand.

decisions.choice: he gave understanding: he instructed me
decisions.reason: The verb means to make someone understand. Some ancient translations read "he came" here, a different but similar word.

decisions.choice: Gabriel's words in quotation marks
decisions.reason: Gabriel's speech, set in double quotation marks, runs to the end of verse 27.

records.source: בִּתְחִלַּ֨ת תַּחֲנוּנֶ֜יךָ יָצָ֣א דָבָ֗ר וַאֲנִי֙ בָּ֣אתִי לְהַגִּ֔יד כִּ֥י חֲמוּד֖וֹת אָ֑תָּה וּבִין֙ בַּדָּבָ֔ר וְהָבֵ֖ן בַּמַּרְאֶֽה׃
records.gloss: At [the] beginning of your supplications a word went out, and I have come to tell, for precious [are] you; and understand the word and have understanding in the vision.
pieces: As soon as you began to plead, an answer was given, and I have come to tell it to you, for you are greatly loved. So pay attention to the message and understand the vision.

L.23: At the beginning of your pleas a word went out, and I have come to tell [it], for you are greatly loved. So consider the word and understand the vision.

R.23: As soon as you began to pray, God gave an answer. I have come to tell it to you, because God loves you very much. So think about this message and understand the vision.

decisions.choice: a word went out: a command or answer was given in heaven
decisions.reason: "Word" may be God's answer to the prayer or his command to Gabriel. It went out at once, at the start of the prayer.

decisions.choice: you are greatly loved: you are precious, highly treasured
decisions.reason: The word means something desired and precious (Genesis 27:15; 2 Chronicles 20:25). The same is said of Daniel in 10:11 and 19. It is God who treasures him.

decisions.choice: the vision: the revelation that follows
decisions.reason: The "vision" is the message about the seventy sevens (verses 24-27), which comes as words, not as a picture.

decisions.choice: God gave an answer; God loves you (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says who gave the word and who loves Daniel; the Hebrew leaves both implied.

records.source: שָׁבֻעִ֨ים שִׁבְעִ֜ים נֶחְתַּ֥ךְ עַֽל־עַמְּךָ֣׀וְעַל־עִ֣יר קָדְשֶׁ֗ךָ לְכַלֵּ֨א הַפֶּ֜שַׁע וּלְהָתֵ֤ם חַטָּאת֙ וּלְכַפֵּ֣ר עָוֺ֔ן וּלְהָבִ֖יא צֶ֣דֶק עֹֽלָמִ֑ים וְלַחְתֹּם֙ חָז֣וֹן וְנָבִ֔יא וְלִמְשֹׁ֖חַ קֹ֥דֶשׁ קָֽדָשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: Sevens seventy have been decreed for your people and for your holy city, to finish the transgression and to seal up sin and to atone for iniquity and to bring righteousness of perpetuity and to seal up vision and prophet and to anoint a holy of holies.
pieces: Seventy sevens have been decreed for your people and your holy city, to put an end to rebellion, to bring sin to a close, to atone for wrongdoing, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to put a seal on vision and prophecy, and to anoint a most holy place.

L.24: Seventy sevens have been decreed for your people and for your holy city: to finish the transgression, and to seal up sin, and to atone for iniquity, and to bring everlasting righteousness, and to seal vision and prophet, and to anoint a most holy [place].

R.24: God has set a time of seventy sets of seven for your people and your holy city. In that time God will end their rebellion. He will finish with sin. He will take away guilt. He will bring in righteousness that will last forever. He will make the vision and the prophecy come true. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will set apart a most holy place for God.

decisions.choice: seventy sevens: the number of periods, and the readings of 9:24-27
decisions.reason: The text gives the number and no unit: "sevens". The usual reading is seventy periods of seven years, 490 years, an extension of Jeremiah's seventy years (verse 2) by seven, perhaps after Leviticus 26:18, 21, 24, 28 ("seven times" for sins) and the sabbath years of Leviticus 25. How the 490 years are counted, and from when, is not stated. The "anointed one" of verses 25-26 has been read in several main ways: as Joshua the high priest of the return (Zechariah 3; 6:11), or Zerubbabel; as Cyrus, whom Isaiah 45:1 calls the LORD's anointed; as Onias III, the high priest killed in 171 BC, in the reading that places the last seven in the time of Antiochus IV; and, in Christian readings, as Jesus the Messiah, whose death is seen in "an anointed one will be cut off" (verse 26). The text settles none of these, and the translation does not choose among them.

decisions.choice: to finish the transgression, to seal up sin: to bring sin to an end
decisions.reason: "Finish" may mean to complete or to restrain. For "seal up", the Hebrew text as written reads "to seal up" (as later in the verse) and the text as read aloud reads "to bring to an end". Both say that the time of sin and its punishment will be closed.

decisions.choice: to seal up vision and prophet: to confirm the prophecy by fulfilling it
decisions.reason: To seal is to authenticate and to close. The vision and the prophet (that is, prophecy) will be confirmed when what they foretold comes to pass.

decisions.choice: to anoint a most holy place: the dedication of a holy place, or a holy person
alternatives: to anoint a most holy one
decisions.reason: "Holy of holies" (most holy) is used of the inner room of the tabernacle and temple, the altar and holy things (Exodus 26:33; 29:37; Ezekiel 45:3), never elsewhere of a person. So it is usually read as the consecration of the temple or its altar, in the usual reading the rededication of 164 BC or the restored temple of the end. Christian readers have also seen in it the anointing of Christ, the Holy One.

decisions.choice: seventy sevens (L, B); seventy sets of seven (R)
decisions.reason: The wording follows the table for Daniel. "Sevens" keeps the Hebrew's lack of a unit (m1); Readable says "sets of seven" so that the number is not misread as seventy times seven. Literal brackets "place" in "a most holy [place]".

decisions.choice: God has set; God will ... He will (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who decreed the time and will do these things; the Hebrew uses a passive and infinitives. The pronoun "he" in these sentences is God's: plain "He" at the start of a sentence, and the deity_pronoun setting in the last sentence.

records.source: וְתֵדַ֨ע וְתַשְׂכֵּ֜ל מִן־מֹצָ֣א דָבָ֗ר לְהָשִׁיב֙ וְלִבְנ֤וֹת יְרֽוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ עַד־מָשִׁ֣יחַ נָגִ֔יד שָׁבֻעִ֖ים שִׁבְעָ֑ה וְשָׁבֻעִ֞ים שִׁשִּׁ֣ים וּשְׁנַ֗יִם תָּשׁוּב֙ וְנִבְנְתָה֙ רְח֣וֹב וְחָר֔וּץ וּבְצ֖וֹק הָעִתִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And you will know and you will understand: from [the] going out of [the] word to restore and to build Jerusalem until an anointed one, a prince, sevens seven; and sevens sixty and two it will again be built, square and moat, and in distress of the times.
pieces: Know and understand this: from the time the word goes out to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until an anointed leader comes, there will be seven sevens. Then for sixty-two sevens it will be rebuilt, with streets and a trench, but in troubled times.

L.25: So know and understand: from the going out of the word to restore and to rebuild Jerusalem until an anointed one, a prince, [there will be] seven sevens. And for sixty-two sevens it will be built again, with plaza and moat, but in times of distress.

R.25: You must know and understand this. A command will be given to rebuild Jerusalem. From that time until a chosen leader comes, there will be seven sets of seven. Then for sixty-two sets of seven, Jerusalem will be rebuilt, with streets and a moat, but in times of trouble.

decisions.choice: until an anointed one, a prince: seven sevens. Then sixty-two sevens
alternatives: until an anointed one, a prince, there will be seven sevens and sixty-two sevens; it will be built again ...
decisions.reason: The Hebrew accents put the main pause of the verse after "seven sevens", so that the anointed prince comes after seven sevens, and the sixty-two sevens are the time in which the city is rebuilt. The translation follows that division. Read without the accents, the two numbers can be joined: "until an anointed one, a prince, [there will be] seven sevens and sixty-two sevens", sixty-nine sevens in all, which is how many Christian readers, following some ancient translations, have counted to the coming of Christ. See the note at verse 24.

decisions.choice: the going out of the word to restore and rebuild Jerusalem: the starting point of the count
decisions.reason: The "word" may be God's word (like the word of verse 23, or Jeremiah's prophecy of verse 2, given in 597 or 587 BC), or a king's decree: that of Cyrus (538 BC; Ezra 1:1-4), or later decrees under Artaxerxes (Ezra 7; Nehemiah 2, about 458 or 445 BC). The readings of verse 24 count from different starting points.

decisions.choice: an anointed one, a prince: an anointed leader
decisions.reason: Both words lack the article. "Anointed" is used of kings, priests and once of Cyrus (Isaiah 45:1); "prince" (nagid) means a leader or ruler, used of kings (1 Samuel 9:16) and of a chief priest (Nehemiah 11:11). On who is meant, see verse 24.

decisions.choice: plaza and moat: the open square and the defenses of the city
decisions.reason: The first word means the open square inside the gate; the second, a word found only here in the Bible, is usually taken as a trench or moat. Together they say the city will be fully rebuilt.

decisions.choice: an anointed one, a prince (L); an anointed leader (B); a chosen leader (R); no deity pronoun
decisions.reason: The wording follows the table for Daniel; Readable says "chosen" for anointed, as in Isaiah 45:1. The anointed one takes no deity_pronoun span, since the text does not settle who he is (verse 24).

decisions.choice: seven sevens, sixty-two sevens (L, B); sets of seven (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 24.

records.source: וְאַחֲרֵ֤י הַשָּׁבֻעִים֙ שִׁשִּׁ֣ים וּשְׁנַ֔יִם יִכָּרֵ֥ת מָשִׁ֖יחַ וְאֵ֣ין ל֑וֹ וְהָעִ֨יר וְהַקֹּ֜דֶשׁ יַ֠שְׁחִית עַ֣ם נָגִ֤יד הַבָּא֙ וְקִצּ֣וֹ בַשֶּׁ֔טֶף וְעַד֙ קֵ֣ץ מִלְחָמָ֔ה נֶחֱרֶ֖צֶת שֹׁמֵמֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And after the sevens sixty and two will be cut off an anointed one, and nothing [will be] to him; and the city and the sanctuary will destroy [the] people of a prince who is coming; and its end [will be] with the flood, and until [the] end war; [the] determined [things are] desolations.
pieces: After the sixty-two sevens an anointed one will be cut off, left with nothing. The people of the ruler who is to come will destroy the city and the sanctuary. Its end will come like a flood, and war will continue to the end; desolations have been decreed.

L.26: And after the sixty-two sevens an anointed one will be cut off and will have nothing; and the city and the sanctuary the people of a prince who is to come will destroy. And its end [will come] with a flood, and to the end there will be war; desolations are decreed.

R.26: After the sixty-two sets of seven, someone who has been anointed will be killed and will have nothing. Then the army of a ruler who will come will destroy the city and the temple. The end will come like a flood. There will be war until the end. God has decided that there will be terrible destruction.

decisions.choice: an anointed one will be cut off: put to death or removed from office
decisions.reason: "Cut off" is used of being killed (Genesis 9:11; Jeremiah 11:19) and of being removed. On who the anointed one is, see verse 24: readers have taken him as Onias III, killed in 171 BC, or as Jesus the Messiah, among others.

decisions.choice: and will have nothing: a short and hard phrase
alternatives: and no one will be with him
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "and there is not to him". It may mean that he will have nothing (no kingdom, no help), or that he will have no one, or, as some ancient translations take it, that it will be "not for himself". Some think a word is missing.

decisions.choice: the people of the prince who is to come: the forces of a coming ruler
decisions.reason: "Prince" (nagid) is the word used in verse 25, but this is a different ruler, who destroys the city. In the usual reading he is Antiochus IV, whose forces attacked Jerusalem and defiled the sanctuary; others see the Romans, who destroyed the temple in AD 70. The text names no one.

decisions.choice: its end with a flood: an overwhelming end
decisions.reason: A flood is a picture of an army sweeping over a land (Isaiah 8:7-8; 11:22). "Its end" may be the city's or the prince's.

decisions.choice: someone who has been anointed will be killed (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "killed" for "cut off", the sense that most readers take, and "someone who has been anointed" so as not to say whether this is the same anointed one as in verse 25. No deity_pronoun span is used (verse 25).

decisions.choice: the army of a ruler; God has decided (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "army" for the people of the ruler, and names God as the one who decreed the desolations.

records.source: וְהִגְבִּ֥יר בְּרִ֛ית לָרַבִּ֖ים שָׁב֣וּעַ אֶחָ֑ד וַחֲצִ֨י הַשָּׁב֜וּעַ יַשְׁבִּ֣ית׀זֶ֣בַח וּמִנְחָ֗ה וְעַ֨ל כְּנַ֤ף שִׁקּוּצִים֙ מְשֹׁמֵ֔ם וְעַד־כָּלָה֙ וְנֶ֣חֱרָצָ֔ה תִּתַּ֖ךְ עַל־שֹׁמֵֽם׃פ
records.gloss: And he will make strong a covenant with the many [for] seven one; and [in the] middle of the seven he will make cease sacrifice and offering; and on a wing of abominations [will be] one desolating, and until complete destruction, and what is determined will be poured out on the desolated.
pieces: He will make a firm covenant with many for one seven. In the middle of the seven he will put a stop to sacrifice and offering. And on a wing of the temple will be the abomination that brings ruin, until the end that has been decreed is poured out on the one who brings ruin."

L.27: And he will make a strong covenant with the many for one seven; and in the middle of the seven he will put an end to sacrifice and offering. And on a wing of abominations [will come] one who makes desolate, until the complete destruction that is decreed is poured out on the one who makes desolate."

R.27: That ruler will make a strong agreement with many people for one set of seven years. But halfway through that time he will stop the sacrifices and offerings. He will set up the horrible thing that brings ruin on a high part of the temple. He will do this until the end that God has decided is poured out on him."

decisions.choice: he will make a strong covenant: the coming prince of verse 26
decisions.reason: The nearest person before "he" is the prince who is to come (verse 26), and most read it so: a ruler who makes a firm agreement with many, then breaks it. In the usual reading this is Antiochus IV, supported by Jews who abandoned the covenant (11:30-32; 1 Maccabees 1:11-15). Some Christian readers take "he" to be the anointed one, who confirms a covenant; others, a final enemy at the end. The text does not settle it.

decisions.choice: he will put an end to sacrifice and offering
decisions.reason: The stopping of the temple sacrifices is the act of the small horn in 8:11 and of the king in 11:31 and 12:11. In the usual reading it is the suppression of the temple worship by Antiochus IV in 167 BC, about three and a half years before the temple was cleansed (compare "a time, times and half a time", 7:25).

decisions.choice: on a wing of abominations, one who makes desolate: the abomination that makes desolate
decisions.reason: The phrase is the one taken up in 11:31 and 12:11, "the abomination that makes desolate", here in a fuller and harder form. "Abominations" is the word used for idols and idolatrous things (1 Kings 11:5; 2 Kings 23:13). "Wing" may mean a high part or corner of the temple, or the wing of the altar, or the abominations may be pictured as borne on wings; some ancient translations read "on the temple". The usual reading sees the pagan altar set up on the altar of burnt offering in 167 BC (1 Maccabees 1:54, which uses the same phrase).

decisions.choice: the abomination that makes desolate: Matthew 24:15 and Mark 13:14
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of "the abomination of desolation, spoken of through Daniel the prophet" standing in the holy place, as a sign for those in Judea to flee (Matthew 24:15; Mark 13:14). He takes up Daniel's words for what was still to come. The Gospels quote the Greek form of the phrase.

decisions.choice: on the one who makes desolate: the destroyer is himself destroyed
decisions.reason: The last word is the same verb as before: the end that God has decreed falls on the desolator. Some read it as "on the desolate", meaning the ruined city, but the first fits the end of the small horn and the king (7:26; 8:25; 11:45).

decisions.choice: on a wing of abominations [will come] one who makes desolate (L); the abomination that brings ruin (B); the horrible thing that brings ruin (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the table's wording for the phrase, the wording of Matthew 24:15 at those levels (and of Mark 13:14 at Balanced). Literal follows the fuller Hebrew of this verse, with its plural "abominations" and "one who makes desolate", which the table's Literal wording, "the abomination that makes desolate", gives where the Hebrew has the short form (11:31; 12:11).

decisions.choice: That ruler; seven years; a high part of the temple; God has decided (R)
decisions.reason: Readable takes the usual readings of m1 and m3 and says them plainly; they are uncertain, as the meaning decisions say. It says "seven years" for "one seven", the usual reading of the unit (verse 24).
